title: Complete the square
goal: Change x² + bx into a perfect square, then solve with square roots.
generalHint: Look at the tiles. Add (b/2)² to the two sides. Then take both square roots.

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: Solve x² = 7
screens.prompt: Solve the equation. Give all solutions. Type them with a comma.

answer.correctWhy: Both √7 and −√7 have a square of 7.

mistakes.reply: Two numbers have a square of 7. Which other number works?
Two numbers have a square of 7. Which other number works?

steps.text: Two numbers have a square of 7.
The root sign gives the positive root. Add the mirror number.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: A corner for a square
screens.prompt: The picture shows $x^2$ and two strips. Each strip is 3 wide. Together they make $x^2 + 6x$. Move the orange corner into the gap. Guess its size.

followUp.question: Which corner makes a full square?

options.label: A 6 × 6 square
options.reply: Look at the tiles. The corner is 3 × 3. Use (b/2)².

options.label: A 9 × 9 square
options.reply: Look at the tiles. The gap is as wide as a strip. A strip is 3 wide.

feedback.correctWhy: The gap is as wide as the strips, and the strips are 3 wide. The corner has area 9.

hints: Look at the gap. It has the same width as a strip.
screens.caption: Move the corner, choose an answer, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: The square is complete
screens.prompt: Put the 3 × 3 corner in the gap. The four parts make one big square with side $x + 3$. Say which equation is true.

options.label: $x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x+6)^2$
options.reply: The side of the big square is x + 3, not x + 6. Look at the picture.

options.label: $x^2 + 6x + 36 = (x+3)^2$
options.reply: The corner has area 9, not 36. Look at the picture.

feedback.correctWhy: The big square has side x + 3. Its parts are x², two strips of 3x, and the corner 9.

hints: The corner has area 9. The side of the big square is $x+3$.
screens.caption: Move the corner, choose an answer, then check.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Complete the square
screens.prompt: To complete $x^2 + bx$, add $(b/2)^2$. The new left side is the square $(x + b/2)^2$. Lang adds the same number to the two sides of the equation.

screens.label: TRY IT
screens.title: What do you add?
screens.prompt: Complete the square for $x^2 + 10x$. Find the number to add.

answer.correctWhy: Half of 10 is 5. The square of 5 is 25.

mistakes.reply: Look at the tiles. The corner is (b/2) × (b/2). Use (b/2)², not b².
5 is half of 10. The corner has area 5 × 5. What is 5²?

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Solve x² + 6x = 7
screens.prompt: Add 9 to the two sides. The left side becomes $(x+3)^2$. Then $(x+3)^2 = 16$. Take the square root. Solve for $x$.

answer.correctWhy: (x + 3)² = 16 gives x + 3 = 4 or x + 3 = −4. So x = 1 or x = −7.

mistakes.reply: A square of 16 has two roots. Use ±4.
A square of 16 has two roots. Use ±4.
The balance tips. Add 9 to the two sides.

steps.text: The left side is a square.
Both 4 and −4 have a square of 16.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Solve x² − 3x + 1 = 0
screens.prompt: First write $x^2 - 3x = -1$. Half of 3 is 3/2. Add $(3/2)^2 = 9/4$ to the two sides. Then $(x - 3/2)^2 = 5/4$. Solve for $x$.

mistakes.reply: A square of 5/4 has two roots. Use ±.
A square of 5/4 has two roots. Use ±.

hints: Type (3 + sqrt(5))/2, (3 - sqrt(5))/2 or use ±: (3 ± sqrt(5))/2.

steps.text: The left side is a square.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: No real solution
screens.prompt: Look at $x^2 + 4x + 5 = 0$. Add 4 to $x^2 + 4x = -5$. You get $(x+2)^2 = -1$. A square is never negative.

interaction.question: How many real solutions does $(x+2)^2 = -1$ have?

options.label: One
options.reply: A square is never negative. Is there a number whose square is −1?

options.label: Two
options.reply: A square is never negative. Is there a number whose square is −1?

feedback.correctWhy: If the right side is negative, no real number has that square. The equation has no real solution.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: A number before x²
screens.prompt: In $2x^2 - 3x - 5 = 0$, the number 2 stands before $x^2$. The method needs $x^2$ alone. Choose the first step.

options.label: Add 9/4 to the left side
options.reply: First divide by 2, so that x² stands alone. Then add (b/2)² to the two sides.

options.label: Take the square root of both sides
options.reply: Not yet. The left side is not a square.

feedback.correctWhy: The equation becomes x² − (3/2)x − 5/2 = 0. Now the method of the last screens works.

hints: Compare with $x^2 + bx$. Here $x^2$ has the number 2 before it.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Solve 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0
screens.prompt: After the division: $x^2 - \tfrac{3}{2}x = \tfrac{5}{2}$. Add $(3/4)^2 = 9/16$ to the two sides. Then $(x - 3/4)^2 = 49/16$. Solve for $x$.

mistakes.reply: A square of 49/16 has two roots. Use ±7/4.
A square of 49/16 has two roots. Use ±7/4.

steps.text: Add 9/16 to the two sides. Here 5/2 + 9/16 = 49/16.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 2
screens.title: Solve x² − 8x = 9
screens.prompt: Complete the square. Solve the equation. Type all solutions with a comma.

answer.correctWhy: (x − 4)² = 25 gives x − 4 = ±5. So x = 9 or x = −1.

mistakes.reply: A square of 25 has two roots. Use ±5.
A square of 25 has two roots. Use ±5.
The balance tips. Add 16 to the two sides, not only to the left side.

hints: Half of 8 is 4. Add $4^2 = 16$ to the two sides.

steps.text: The left side is a square.
Both 5 and −5 have a square of 25.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 2
screens.title: Solve x² + 2x − 4 = 0
screens.prompt: Complete the square. Type the solutions. You can use ±, for example -1 ± sqrt(5).

mistakes.reply: A square of 5 has two roots. Use ±√5.
A square of 5 has two roots. Use ±√5.
Look at the sign. (x + 1)² = 5 gives x + 1 = ±√5. Subtract 1.

hints: Write $x^2 + 2x = 4$. Add 1 to the two sides.

steps.text: The left side is a square.

feedback.correctWhy: Both 4 and −4 have a square of 16. A square root gives two numbers.
